newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline near session lows late, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline near session lows late, volume thin.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline hovered about session lows Friday afternoon in thin trade though dealers expected crude to gather strength after holding trendline support, stemming furth losses in gasoline.
"If we keep above $19.60 in crude, we should be okay in gasoline, otherwise gasoline will drop even more," said a New York gasoline trader.

At 1431 EDT, June gasoline was off 1.83 cents at 60.80 cents a gallon. June crude was off 29 cents at $19.62 a barrel after holding trendline support that extends from the April 10 low and the low April 17 on the spot chart.
June gasoline had fallen as low as 60.50 cents.
"The cracks had become really expensive, and there were sell stops that were triggered in 0.10 cent increments after 61.50 cents," said a New York refined products dealer.
The June gasoline-to-crude crack spread had fallen to $6.00 a barrel from $6.39 Thursday and $6.63 Wednesday.
Dealers said spot gasoline should hold the 60.00 cent level in the near term as it represents good value amid the seasonally strongest period for demand.
"60.00 cent gasoline in June is pretty good value since that is after Memorial Day weekend," said a dealer, noting a popular driving holiday.
June heating oil was off 1.38 cents a gallon at 52.95 cents gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
